  - Calorie strategy: start at maintenance with slight surplus on heavier training days to support lean mass gain; adjust weekly based on progress and climber performance.
  - Protein: 1.8–2.4 g/kg bodyweight per day, distributed across 3–5 meals; emphasize leucine-rich sources (whey, chicken, fish, eggs, tofu, legumes).
  - Carbohydrates: target 3–5 g/kg on training days to fuel sessions; adjust downward on rest days to support recomposition.
  - Fats: ~0.8–1.0 g/kg to support hormones and overall energy.
  - Meal timing: protein spaced 3–4 hours; post-workout protein + carb within 1–2 hours.
  - Hydration: aim for 30–35 ml/kg/day; adjust with sweat loss; include electrolytes on long/climbing days.
  - Nutrient quality: prioritize whole foods, vegetables, fiber, and micronutrient density; limit added sugars.
  - Adjustments: weekly check-ins for weight, performance, energy, recovery; adjust calories by +/- 100–200 kcal as needed.
  - Supplements (optional): whey or plant-based protein if protein targets not met; vitamin D and omega-3 status considered; consult clinician if using any medications.

  - All exercises stay within pain-free ROM with no overhead loading as per constraint.
  - Mobility work integrated daily; sessions include targeted shoulder, thoracic, hip, ankle, and soft-tissue release.
  - Cardio additions are 2x/week, structured to support endurance for longer climbing days without compromising shoulder health.
  - Hangboard & climbing prep are introduced in Phase 1 and progressively increased; Phase 3 includes peak-intensity emphasis and climbing-trip readiness with controlled grip loading within pain-free ROM.
  - Peak intensity in Phase 3 Week 9–12 is designed to crest by Week 12 to align with climbing trip window, with deloads and recovery focus surrounding the peak.
  - Saturday Finisher: Phase 1 introduces a weekly Saturday full-body finisher for enjoyment and work capacity; phases 2–3 retain variant finisher ideas as appropriate.
  - Phase 1 Cardio Boost and Phase 2/Cardio phases are integrated to support climbing endurance without overloading shoulder health.
  - Phase 1 Hangboard intro to Phase 3 peak progression with climbing-specific prep planned to ensure shoulder safety.
